cells.tense: The way is being shown clearly, and the pen is still moving on the page.
cells.act: make something skilled and small on the cleared ground
cells.ask: Where a false plan has come down lately and left open ground, make the first thing by hand — a page, a route, a joined joint. Leave it finished where the old one stood, and don't rebuild underneath it this week.
cells.core:
You can put a direction in front of someone and they will follow it. The mind finds the passage; the body holds the weight of the walk while they learn the way, and you don't need the credit or the speed. Some old false route has come down lately and left open ground behind it, and what belongs there is clearer to you than to anyone nearby.

The balance holds while you keep making and stop re-litigating the clearing. Nobody needs the old route back; they need the finished first step to stand on. Keep the pen on the new page and the old one closes cleanly. That is what this balance is free to feed next — the next piece built, not the last one defended.

cells.tense: A future is being held at a distance by carrying the whole crossing alone.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Stop walking around the hard part — the conversation, the draft, the number — and walk straight into it on purpose, once. See what actually holds under your hands and what was only bracing. Set the bracing down.
cells.core:
You are braced for the moment the route falls through, so you take the whole crossing onto your own back before anyone else has to hold any of it. The next instruction arrives before the first has been tried. The mind keeps finding passage faster than legs can walk, and the gap between them is the load you are carrying.

What gives under that is not the direction. It is the willingness of the people walking it to keep pointing themselves. Engage the hard thing once and find out which parts of the plan are real. Release the method; nothing about the purpose is what is failing.

cells.tense: The place where you stopped pointing the way is behind you now.
cells.act: return the small thing you owe before anyone asks
cells.ask: A debt sits somewhere nearby — a reply, a returned thing, a word not said. Return it before anyone has to ask, and say nothing about having done it. No one needs the accounting, and nobody checked.
cells.core:
The passage stays visible to you. The instinct to point it out has gone quiet, and the standing still is doing the work now. Nothing is being carried or held. What held under pressure before is being saved, and saving it keeps it out of use — no one crosses because no one is being shown.

Let the private compass handle the case at hand. You do not need the strength to carry a whole crossing again. You need the fair act where nobody is watching and the thing owed is plain to you. The current comes back through the act, not through waiting to feel equal to it first. The compass knows the case. Take it.

cells.tense: The route is being walked while the one who charted it stays unnamed behind the pen.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Take the direction you have been carrying alone and bring someone onto the actual work of it — the next step, not the whole route. Do that piece together, both hands in it, and move on from wherever that leaves you.
cells.core:
You charted the crossing and the people on it are walking it, and the fact that the chart came from you has gone quiet in your own accounting. Nothing in your day needs the credit back. That is not the point. The point is that a direction kept private cannot be corrected, helped, or joined, and you are the only one holding the shape of where it goes.

Bring someone onto the work itself — not the load, not the whole route, just the next step — and do it with them. Two streams running as one for an afternoon. You do not have to become the person who claims the chart; you only have to let another set a hand on the same piece and go on from there.
cells.sheetLine: You made the way. Do the next piece with someone.

attempts.check: The seat is Fortitude (endurance, holding capacity), but the drawing card is Guidance — discipline through the mind, pointing others toward the way. I cannot claim the person is carrying a specific load, has been for a specific time, or knows what it costs; the record gives me only the capacity pattern. The reader could reasonably say 'I don't feel like I'm holding anything up' — if that is true, the Too Much bridge collapses and the ask becomes the only thing left. The ask still works if the read is wrong, because it is small, bounded, and teaches the person something about how they engage friction regardless of whether the diagnosis lands. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that keeps 'holding others up' as a universal — the record only licenses one reversible example, and I have narrowed it to 'tonight' where I need the reader to be able to say no.
